audit.reason: The bundled test certs have no Authority Key Identifier, so the default strict chain checks reject them. The repo's own test helper (tests/util.py:38) sets verifier._chain_verifier.enable_strict_checks = False for this reason ('We don't have authority identifiers on test certs'), and with that setting the repo's notification-decoding test passes here. The oracle builds the verifier without disabling strict checks, and the README never says Apple's test certs pass strict verification, so the bug is in the oracle; the signature part already passed.
